what_happened: The operator wrote acceptance criteria for several jobs that were wrong. Two would have failed correct work: job 5b's criterion (2026-10-17), and job 9bw7's criterion 9, which banned the changelog entry that Athena's own default adds. One would have allowed the wrong thing: zvmr's criterion 3 allowed interventions after the landing commit. Two of the three were caught only when someone read the reading closely. The operator logged this as their own mistake.
cause: Criteria are written as free text, by the operator or by the reader. No stage compares them with Athena's own defaults and invariants, such as the changelog default and the rules for landing and interventions. The defaults live in code and docs apart from the reading. A contradiction therefore shows up only if a human reads the reading closely, or when the verifier rejects the work at the end. The critic checks plans, not the criteria themselves.
prevention: Add a criteria-lint step at reading acceptance. It would hold a machine-readable list of Athena's default side effects and invariants: the changelog entry added by default, landing-commit ordering, and no interventions after landing. Each criterion would be checked against that list. A criterion that forbids a default output, or permits something an invariant forbids, would block acceptance and name the conflicting default. The reader or critic prompt would also be told to run this check and list its findings.
proposed_request: Add a check at reading acceptance that compares each acceptance criterion with Athena's own defaults and invariants. Cover at least: the default changelog entry that every job adds, the landing rules, and the rule that no intervention may be recorded after the landing commit. When a criterion would fail work that follows those defaults, or would allow something the invariants forbid, the reading should be refused with a message that names the criterion and the default or invariant it conflicts with. Show the check working on three cases. One criterion bans the changelog. One allows interventions after the landing commit. One is consistent with the defaults and passes.
